name: Linear Algebra: Vectrine
subtitle: Linear Algebra course and quiz
shortDescription: Adaptive linear algebra course with five 3D labs: eigen-axes, SVD compression, least squares, PageRank and vibration modes. Chosen-length quizzes. Free to use.
longDescription:
Vectrine is a free, adaptive linear algebra course for college students and self-learners. It covers systems of equations and row reduction, matrices and inverses, determinants, vector spaces (span, basis, dimension, rank and nullity), linear transformations, orthogonality, projections and least squares, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, symmetric matrices and the singular value decomposition (SVD).

### Five 3D Labs
Start from a real problem and explore it in 3D: a strained rock and its eigen-axes, a terrain tile compressed by SVD, a survey plane fitted by least squares, route surfers ranking a network by PageRank, and a footbridge's vibration modes. Each lab shows live formulas and a second method that checks the answer, and opens its cited sources in an in-app window.

### Your Level, Your Length
Pick 5, 10, 20, 40 or your own number of questions, from beginner to research-level, adaptive or in course order. Mock exams stay ad-free.

### Practice that adapts to you
The app tracks mastery per topic, spots the specific mistake pattern behind each wrong answer, and chooses your next question from those mistakes, with spaced review. Switch to the traditional curriculum order any time.

### Learn by doing
Four interactive labs (a grid morpher with an SVD mode, an eigenvector explorer, a row-reduction stepper and a least-squares fitter), more than 190 original questions with worked solutions, unit checkpoints and timed mock exams. Tap any concept for an explanation from K-12 level up to graduate level. Every topic links to further study such as MIT OpenCourseWare, Khan Academy and 3Blue1Brown. All questions and explanations are original; sources are linked, never copied.

Free with ads at natural breaks, with an optional monthly ad-free plan. Not affiliated with any university or listed source.
